svg.title: DIA-201 · A load line, repainted
svg.desc: An engraved plate of a riveted ship's hull seen from the side, with cargo stacked on deck and one more crate being lowered. Four load-line marks are painted on the hull in a rising column. The lowest, dated autumn 2023, is far under water and struck through. Two more above it are also submerged and struck through. The newest, in rust, sits just above the waterline.
svg.text: PART II · WHY YOU FEEL HELPLESS
cargo taken on to keep pace
autumn 2023, first painted: pause if capability outruns control
third repainting, by February 2026: no pause. April 2026: a fresh coat, same height.
The Merchant Shipping Act of 1876 made the mark compulsory, and left its height to the owner.
DIA-201 · A standard set by the one it binds follows the water.
